title: Generic Result Type and Exhaustive Event Handling
instructions: Implement `Ok`, `Err`, `is_ok`, `map_result`, `unwrap_or`, `parse_int` and `describe` in `results.py`. `Ok` and `Err` must be frozen, slotted dataclasses, `map_result` passes an `Err` through as the same object, and `describe` ends its if/elif chain with `assert_never`. The event TypedDicts are provided. Strict type-checking (`mypy --strict`, narrowing with `TypeIs`) is self-checked; the hidden tests grade runtime behaviour.

evidence.label: parse_int returns Ok for integers and Err("not an int: ...") otherwise
parse_int handles whitespace, negatives, empty and decimal strings
map_result transforms an Ok and returns the same Err object untouched
map_result never calls the function for an Err
is_ok is True for Ok, False for Err
unwrap_or returns the value or the default, even for falsy values
Ok and Err are frozen, hashable and slotted
describe maps token, tool_call and done events to their labels
describe raises AssertionError for an unknown event type
